scope: MILESTONE 5 / BREAKTHROUGH: with an empty snapshot first and an entity snapshot afterwards, the client sits in state 10 WITH one entity in its list

the_method.effect: the first snapshots carry no entity, later ones carry the mode-1 entity with its position float
the_method.probe: 0x6716AD:IdStore fired once, so the entity was decoded by the client

why_this_is_the_breakthrough: until now every single body with count = 1 ended at state 9, and every body that reached state 10 had count = 0
that looked like a contradiction: the client seemed to refuse the in-match state while any entity existed
the resolution is ORDER: the client leaves the loading screen on a snapshot with no entities, and only then accepts snapshots that add entities
which is exactly how a real server behaves - the gamestate and first snapshots establish the world, entities appear afterwards
what_this_means_for_the_project: the entity pipeline is now demonstrably compatible with the in-match state
the remaining question is no longer whether the client accepts our entities, but whether it DRAWS them
and drawing needs a screenshot check, which the next verification step must do
next: run the same alternating sequence and take a screenshot at t=50..65 to see whether the entity is visible
if the frame is still black, the next layer is the render-side state (a view entity / clientNum tie) rather than the snapshot contents
